audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Samson Timnah marriage, lion and honey, feast, riddle, coercion, and Ashkelon killing narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for intermarriage/uncircumcised rhetoric, ambiguous Divine occasion clause, lion and carcass episodes, wedding-feast companions, riddle wager, threat against Samson's wife, pressure disclosure, heifer metaphor, thirty killings for garments, and transfer of the wife to a companion.

verses.restored: Samson went down to Timnah and saw a woman in Timnah from daughters of Philistines.

familiar.text: And Samson went down to Timnath, and saw a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines.

modern.text: One day Samson went down to Timnah, where he saw a young Philistine woman.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥רֶד שִׁמְשׁ֖וֹן תִּמְנָ֑תָה וַיַּ֥רְא אִשָּׁ֛ה בְּתִמְנָ֖תָה מִבְּנ֥וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: He went up and told his father and his mother and said, I saw a woman in Timnah from daughters of Philistines; now take her for me as wife.

familiar.text: And he came up, and told his father and his mother, and said, I have seen a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines: now therefore get her for me to wife.

modern.text: So he returned and told his father and mother, “I have seen a daughter of the Philistines in Timnah. Now get her for me as a wife.”

original.text: וַיַּ֗עַל וַיַּגֵּד֙ לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אִשָּׁ֛ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְתִמְנָ֖תָה מִבְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וְעַתָּ֕ה קְחוּ אוֹתָ֥הּ לִּ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: His father and his mother said to him, Is there no woman among daughters of your kin or among all my people, that you are going to take a wife from uncircumcised Philistines? Samson said to his father, Take her for me, because she is right in my eyes.

familiar.text: Then his father and his mother said unto him, Is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? And Samson said unto his father, Get her for me; for she pleaseth me well.

modern.text: But his father and mother replied, “Can’t you find a young woman among your relatives or among any of our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?” But Samson told his father, “Get her for me, for she is pleasing to my eyes.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ אָבִ֣יו וְאִמּ֗וֹ הַאֵין֩ בִּבְנ֨וֹת אַחֶ֤יךָ וּבְכָל עַמִּי֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי אַתָּ֤ה הוֹלֵךְ֙ לָקַ֣חַת אִשָּׁ֔ה מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים הָעֲרֵלִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֤וֹן אֶל אָבִיו֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ קַֽח לִ֔י כִּֽי הִ֖יא יָשְׁרָ֥ה בְעֵינָֽי

verses.restored: His father and his mother did not know that this was from YHWH, because he was seeking an occasion from Philistines. At that time Philistines were ruling in Israel.

familiar.text: But his father and his mother knew not that it was of the LORD, that he sought an occasion against the Philistines: for at that time the Philistines had dominion over Israel.

modern.text: (Now his father and mother did not know this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion to move against the Philistines; for at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.)

original.text: וְאָבִ֨יו וְאִמּ֜וֹ לֹ֣א יָדְע֗וּ כִּ֤י מֵיְהוָה֙ הִ֔יא כִּי תֹאֲנָ֥ה הֽוּא מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים מֹשְׁלִ֥ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Samson went down, and his father and his mother, to Timnah. They came as far as vineyards of Timnah, and look—a young lion of lions roared toward him.

familiar.text: Then went Samson down, and his father and his mother, to Timnath, and came to the vineyards of Timnath: and, behold, a young lion roared against him.

modern.text: Then Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother and came to the vineyards of Timnah. Suddenly a young lion came roaring at him,

original.text: וַיֵּ֧רֶד שִׁמְשׁ֛וֹן וְאָבִ֥יו וְאִמּ֖וֹ תִּמְנָ֑תָה וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ עַד כַּרְמֵ֣י תִמְנָ֔תָה וְהִנֵּה֙ כְּפִ֣יר אֲרָי֔וֹת שֹׁאֵ֖ג לִקְרָאתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Spirit of YHWH rushed upon him, and he tore it apart as one tears apart a young goat, though nothing was in his hand. He did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.

familiar.text: And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother what he had done.

modern.text: and the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as one would tear a young goat. But he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.

original.text: וַתִּצְלַ֨ח עָלָ֜יו ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֗ה וַֽיְשַׁסְּעֵ֨הוּ֙ כְּשַׁסַּ֣ע הַגְּדִ֔י וּמְא֖וּמָה אֵ֣ין בְּיָד֑וֹ וְלֹ֤א הִגִּיד֙ לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֔וֹ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה

verses.restored: He went down and spoke with the woman, and she was right in eyes of Samson.

familiar.text: And he went down, and talked with the woman; and she pleased Samson well.

modern.text: Then Samson continued on his way down and spoke to the woman, because she was pleasing to his eyes. Samson’s Riddle

original.text: וַיֵּ֖רֶד וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר לָאִשָּׁ֑ה וַתִּישַׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י שִׁמְשֽׁוֹן

verses.restored: After days he returned to take her, and turned aside to see fallen body of lion. Look—a community/swarm of bees was in body of lion, and honey.

familiar.text: And after a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcase of the lion: and, behold, there was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcase of the lion.

modern.text: When Samson returned later to take her, he left the road to see the lion’s carcass, and in it was a swarm of bees, along with their honey.

original.text: וַיָּ֤שָׁב מִיָּמִים֙ לְקַחְתָּ֔הּ וַיָּ֣סַר לִרְא֔וֹת אֵ֖ת מַפֶּ֣לֶת הָאַרְיֵ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה עֲדַ֧ת דְּבוֹרִ֛ים בִּגְוִיַּ֥ת הָאַרְיֵ֖ה וּדְבָֽשׁ

verses.restored: He scraped it into his palms and went on, walking and eating. He went to his father and his mother and gave to them, and they ate; he did not tell them that from body of lion he scraped honey.

familiar.text: And he took thereof in his hands, and went on eating, and came to his father and mother, and he gave them, and they did eat: but he told not them that he had taken the honey out of the carcase of the lion.

modern.text: So he scooped some honey into his hands and ate it as he went along. And when he returned to his father and mother, he gave some to them and they ate it. But he did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the lion’s carcass.

original.text: וַיִּרְדֵּ֣הוּ אֶל כַּפָּ֗יו וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְאָכֹ֔ל וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֶל אָבִ֣יו וְאֶל אִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם וַיֹּאכֵ֑לוּ וְלֹֽא הִגִּ֣יד לָהֶ֔ם כִּ֛י מִגְּוִיַּ֥ת הָאַרְיֵ֖ה רָדָ֥ה הַדְּבָֽשׁ

verses.restored: His father went down to the woman, and Samson made there a feast, because so young men would do.

familiar.text: So his father went down unto the woman: and Samson made there a feast; for so used the young men to do.

modern.text: Then his father went to visit the woman, and Samson prepared a feast there, as was customary for the bridegroom.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥רֶד אָבִ֖יהוּ אֶל הָאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיַּ֨עַשׂ שָׁ֤ם שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יַעֲשׂ֖וּ הַבַּחוּרִֽים

verses.restored: When they saw him, they took thirty companions, and they were with him.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when they saw him, that they brought thirty companions to be with him.

modern.text: And when the Philistines saw him, they selected thirty men to accompany him.

original.text: וַיְהִ֖י כִּרְאוֹתָ֣ם אוֹת֑וֹ וַיִּקְחוּ֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים מֵֽרֵעִ֔ים וַיִּהְי֖וּ אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Samson said to them, Let me please riddle a riddle to you. If telling, you tell it to me in seven days of feast and find it, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.

familiar.text: And Samson said unto them, I will now put forth a riddle unto you: if ye can certainly declare it me within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I will give you thirty sheets and thirty change of garments:

modern.text: “Let me tell you a riddle,” Samson said to them. “If you can solve it for me within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אָחֽוּדָה נָּ֥א לָכֶ֖ם חִידָ֑ה אִם הַגֵּ֣ד תַּגִּידוּ֩ אוֹתָ֨הּ לִ֜י שִׁבְעַ֨ת יְמֵ֤י הַמִּשְׁתֶּה֙ וּמְצָאתֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָכֶם֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים סְדִינִ֔ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים חֲלִפֹ֥ת בְּגָדִֽים

verses.restored: But if you are not able to tell me, you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing. They said to him, Riddle your riddle, and let us hear it.

familiar.text: But if ye cannot declare it me, then shall ye give me thirty sheets and thirty change of garments. And they said unto him, Put forth thy riddle, that we may hear it.

modern.text: But if you cannot solve it, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.” “Tell us your riddle,” they replied. “Let us hear it.”

original.text: וְאִם לֹ֣א תוּכְלוּ֮ לְהַגִּ֣יד לִי֒ וּנְתַתֶּ֨ם אַתֶּ֥ם לִי֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים סְדִינִ֔ים וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים חֲלִיפ֣וֹת בְּגָדִ֑ים וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֔וֹ ח֥וּדָה חִידָתְךָ֖ וְנִשְׁמָעֶֽנָּה

verses.restored: He said to them, From the eater came food, and from strong came sweet. They were not able to tell the riddle for three days.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness. And they could not in three days expound the riddle.

modern.text: So he said to them: “Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.” For three days they were unable to explain the riddle.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם מֵהָֽאֹכֵל֙ יָצָ֣א מַאֲכָ֔ל וּמֵעַ֖ז יָצָ֣א מָת֑וֹק וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֛וּ לְהַגִּ֥יד הַחִידָ֖ה שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים

verses.restored: On seventh day they said to Samson's wife, Entice your husband so he will tell us the riddle, lest we burn you and house of your father with fire. Did you invite us to dispossess/impoverish us?

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that they said unto Samson’s wife, Entice thy husband, that he may declare unto us the riddle, lest we burn thee and thy father’s house with fire: have ye called us to take that we have? is it not so?

modern.text: So on the fourth day they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband to explain the riddle to us, or we will burn you and your father’s household to death. Did you invite us here to rob us?”

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ לְאֵֽשֶׁת שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ פַּתִּ֣י אֶת אִישֵׁ֗ךְ וְיַגֶּד לָ֨נוּ֙ אֶת הַ֣חִידָ֔ה פֶּן נִשְׂרֹ֥ף אוֹתָ֛ךְ וְאֶת בֵּ֥ית אָבִ֖יךְ בָּאֵ֑שׁ הַלְיָרְשֵׁ֕נוּ קְרָאתֶ֥ם לָ֖נוּ הֲלֹֽא

verses.restored: Samson's wife wept upon him and said, You only hate me and do not love me. You riddled a riddle to sons of my people, but to me you have not told it. He said to her, Look, to my father and my mother I have not told it; and to you should I tell?

familiar.text: And Samson’s wife wept before him, and said, Thou dost but hate me, and lovest me not: thou hast put forth a riddle unto the children of my people, and hast not told it me. And he said unto her, Behold, I have not told it my father nor my mother, and shall I tell it thee?

modern.text: Then Samson’s wife came to him, weeping, and said, “You hate me! You do not really love me! You have posed to my people a riddle, but have not explained it to me.” “Look,” he said, “I have not even explained it to my father or mother, so why should I explain it to you?”

original.text: וַתֵּבְךְּ֩ אֵ֨שֶׁת שִׁמְשׁ֜וֹן עָלָ֗יו וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ רַק שְׂנֵאתַ֨נִי֙ וְלֹ֣א אֲהַבְתָּ֔נִי הַֽחִידָ֥ה חַ֨דְתָּ֙ לִבְנֵ֣י עַמִּ֔י וְלִ֖י לֹ֣א הִגַּ֑דְתָּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הִנֵּ֨ה לְאָבִ֧י וּלְאִמִּ֛י לֹ֥א הִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְלָ֥ךְ אַגִּֽיד

verses.restored: She wept upon him seven days during which the feast was theirs. On seventh day he told her because she pressed him, and she told the riddle to sons of her people.

familiar.text: And she wept before him the seven days, while their feast lasted: and it came to pass on the seventh day, that he told her, because she lay sore upon him: and she told the riddle to the children of her people.

modern.text: She wept the whole seven days of the feast, and finally on the seventh day, because she had pressed him so much, he told her the answer. And in turn she explained the riddle to her people.

original.text: וַתֵּ֤בְךְּ עָלָיו֙ שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם הַמִּשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וַיַּגֶּד לָהּ֙ כִּ֣י הֱצִיקַ֔תְהוּ וַתַּגֵּ֥ד הַחִידָ֖ה לִבְנֵ֥י עַמָּֽהּ

verses.restored: Men of city said to him on seventh day before sun went down, What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than lion? He said to them, If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found my riddle.

familiar.text: And the men of the city said unto him on the seventh day before the sun went down, What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion? And he said unto them, If ye had not plowed with my heifer, ye had not found out my riddle.

modern.text: Before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the city said to Samson: “What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?” So he said to them: “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle!”

familiar.text: And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon, and slew thirty men of them, and took their spoil, and gave change of garments unto them which expounded the riddle. And his anger was kindled, and he went up to his father’s house.

modern.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon, killed thirty of their men, took their apparel, and gave their clothes to those who had solved the riddle. And burning with anger, Samson returned to his father’s house,

modern.text: and his wife was given to one of the men who had accompanied him.

translation_notes: The woman of Timnah is never named. Samson first sees her, then commands his parents to obtain her; her own desire and consent are not narrated.
The term 'uncircumcised Philistines' is ancient boundary polemic and may not authorize ethnic slurs, anti-intermarriage ideology, xenophobia, or contempt for uncircumcised bodies.

Verse 4's pronouns are ambiguous: YHWH or Samson may be the seeker of an occasion. The claim that the situation is 'from YHWH' does not make coercion, killing, or the treatment of the woman as an instrument morally good.
The lion and honey scene involves animal death, corpse contact, secrecy, and possible Nazirite impurity tension; it is not a model for proving strength.
The thirty companions may be wedding attendants, watchers, or a security presence. The text does not explain why they are assigned.
The riddle wager creates economic pressure, but the companions answer it by threatening to burn the woman and her father's house. Her disclosure occurs under credible threat of lethal violence.
Verse 16 records relational pressure between wife and husband, but it must be read alongside the death threat against her. She is not a simple seductress or traitor.
Samson's 'my heifer' metaphor objectifies his wife and casts other men as using her body/labor. Preserve the metaphor as evidence of patriarchal speech, not acceptable relationship language.
Samson kills thirty men in Ashkelon to pay a clothing debt. The Spirit formula reports narrative empowerment but must not be treated as blanket moral approval of revenge or killing uninvolved people.
The wife is transferred to Samson's companion without her voice. Marriage arrangements in this chapter repeatedly deny her bodily and relational autonomy.
safety_note: Do not blame the Timnite woman for disclosing the riddle under an arson-and-death threat. Reject misogynistic readings that make her a stereotype of deceptive women. Do not use Divine providence language to sanctify forced marriage, ethnic hostility, animal cruelty, coercion, revenge killing, theft, or treating a woman as property.
